encounters.cc: Heavy vaginal bleeding that began 30 minutes after vaginal delivery at term

lines: Heavy vaginal bleeding that began 30 minutes after vaginal delivery at term

This 32-year-old female with Von Willebrand disease Type 1 and chronic iron deficiency anemia presents with heavy vaginal bleeding 30 minutes after vaginal delivery, following admission for uterine inversion.
Her pregnancy was largely uneventful, though she had a few episodes of light spotting during third trimester.
She received no ultrasound beyond 20 weeks and had no prenatal complications.
Labor progressed spontaneously without induction, augmentation, or instrumentation, and she delivered a healthy newborn without difficulty.
Placenta was delivered a few minutes later but was noted to have an irregular margin and a vessel extending to the membranes.
Bleeding continues despite administration of oxytocin.
- Kallmann syndrome (isolated hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with anosmia)
- History of infertility secondary to hypogonadism
- Dilation and curettage for retained products of conception
- Desmopressin acetate 150 mcg intranasal spray as needed for bleeding episodes
- Ethinyl estradiol/norethindrone acetate 1 tablet PO daily (continuous cycling for hormone replacement)

The uterus is firm and consistent in size with postpartum expectations.

encounters.cc: Worsening fatigue, difficulty caring for newborn, and low breastmilk production one week after emergency cesarean section

lines: Worsening fatigue, difficulty caring for newborn, and low breastmilk production one week after emergency cesarean section

The patient is a 32-year-old female with Von Willebrand disease Type 1, Kallmann syndrome, and chronic iron deficiency anemia who presents for inpatient evaluation one week after undergoing an emergency cesarean section complicated by acute uterine inversion and postpartum hemorrhage.
The delivery was complicated by significant intraoperative bleeding, during which her blood pressure dropped to 80/40 mm Hg.
She required transfusion of 4 units of packed red blood cells.
Since the surgery, she has experienced worsening fatigue and difficulty caring for her newborn.
She also reports that her breastmilk production has been unusually low despite frequent attempts at breastfeeding.
- Secondary postpartum hemorrhage due to retained products of conception (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Kallmann syndrome (isolated hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with anosmia)
- History of infertility secondary to hypogonadism
- Dilation and curettage for retained products of conception

- Mother: Type 1 Von Willebrand disease, menorrhagia requiring hysterectomy at age 42
- Father: Delayed puberty (age 16), poor sense of smell (presumed variant Kallmann syndrome)
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Librarian.
On physical exam, she appears pale and mildly hypotensive.
Her surgical wound is healing appropriately, and there are no signs of infection.

lines: Postoperative follow-up one week after repeat cesarean section delivery of second child

The patient is a 34-year-old female with Kallmann syndrome and Von Willebrand disease type 1 who returns for postoperative follow-up one week after repeat cesarean section delivery of her second child, following a prior pregnancy complicated by uterine inversion and severe postpartum hemorrhage.
Her delivery was complicated by significant hemorrhage requiring transfusion.
She reports profound fatigue and an inability to produce milk despite frequent attempts at breastfeeding.
She also mentions feeling lightheaded when standing and has had difficulty concentrating.
She notes that she has not had any vaginal bleeding or lochia since delivery.
